_comment: Live state-detection tuning for bin/claude-mate-wrap. Case-insensitive substrings matched against the rendered claude TUI screen. Hot-reloaded (~0.25s), no restart. Precedence: error > waiting > waiting_footer > busy > idle. NOTE: the BACKGROUND-WORK signals are NOT tunable here — the 'Waiting for N ... to finish' banner, the turn recap's '... still running' suffix, the live in-flight chip in the hint row and the task panel's in-background counter are matched by structural regexes in the wrapper (_BG_WORK_RE / _BG_TURN_END_RE / _BG_CHIP_RE / _BG_COUNT_RE) — because a substring loose enough to catch them would fire on ordinary prose, and because the three that live in the TRANSCRIPT are frozen once printed and so are only trusted while nothing Claude printed after them has superseded them (the wrapper's _fresh() gate); the chip is read below the prompt box, where only Claude's own live chrome renders. This is why the banner's phrases ('background agent', 'agent to finish', 'workflow to finish', 'tool to finish') are no longer in 'busy': as bare substrings they had neither the shape nor the freshness gate, so a printed banner kept a finished session on WIP for good. They keep a session 'working' after the turn ends, but they never mask 'waiting': only the foreground spinner vetoes the picker footer. Matching is scoped to Claude's LIVE STATUS REGION: strong 'error'/'waiting' in the bottom ~20 non-empty lines; the spinner 'busy' AND the content-prone 'error_footer' only in the bottom ~8, so error/prompt keywords in scrollback/logs/code/conversation above don't false-trigger. 'error' holds STRONG, specific error UI strings; 'error_footer' holds content-prone error PHRASES — scoped to the tight bottom region and ignored while the live meter shows work, so a phrase printed as content can't stick the session in 'error' (which nags every 5s and, via the keepalive, would never be pruned). Bare HTTP status codes (' 500' etc.) are intentionally absent: they collide with the live token meter ('↓ 500 tokens') and any on-screen number. 'waiting_footer' holds GENERIC question/option-picker phrases matched ONLY in the last ~4 lines, AND (in the wrapper) must persist a few seconds before it counts as waiting, so a picker you open and dismiss doesn't buzz. NOTE: 'esc to cancel' / 'esc to go back' are deliberately NOT here — user-opened config dialogs (the /effort and /model sliders) share that footer, so matching it falsely buzzed the instant you typed /effort. A genuine AskUserQuestion picker carries 'to select' / 'to navigate', which those sliders do not.
